gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-diphylleia: Bold and bookish at once, Happy Monkey draws every stroke at a single width while Diphylleia lets its stems outweigh the hairlines. And that gap between wire-straight lines and a gently contrasted serif is what makes this pairing distinct.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-donegal-one: Wire-bent and loud, Happy Monkey holds its line weight constant from end to end, like a sign twisted from metal. Donegal One, a serif, thins its rounded tops slightly and lets the headline do the shouting.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-gentium-book-plus: Gentium Book Plus reads like a classic serif, with generous openings and lighter horizontals. Happy Monkey is best at bold, uniform curves and stems moving in lockstep, while the body font quietly handles the modest thick-thin work of sentences.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-gfs-didot: GFS Didot has a literary, authoritative feel, its round letters swelling lightly and its curves staying generous. But Happy Monkey, with no pressure swell anywhere, is the real hook, a flat, bold shape beside that gentle text serif rhythm.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-hahmlet: Hahmlet sets a dignified text serif voice, with a faint charcoal-like shadow in its strokes and sturdy joins. Hahmlet would carry a long passage comfortably, while Happy Monkey's laser-etched, constant-width heading stays bold above it.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-im-fell-english-s: Bold, bendy wire up top, antique pressed type below. Happy Monkey is best at steel-cable outlines with no thick-thin shift, while IM Fell English SC, a serif, does its best work in gently thinned diagonals and open throats.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-inria-serif: Happy Monkey's ruler-straight line, with no brush swell anywhere, is the first thing you notice. Inria Serif, a serif with tame contrast and wide-mouthed rounds, would carry a long passage with a dignified, easy rhythm.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-joan: Editorial in mood, Happy Monkey's constant pen pressure sits above Joan's text serif bowls with their gentle weight shifts. Let Joan's size stay modest, since its tempered contrast neither jolts nor flattens.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-junge: Chunky, thick-only outlines up top, then a quiet serif below. Junge's light modulation and generous curves would carry a long passage with dignity, never getting fussy.
gen-gf-happy-monkey-gf-kameron: Kameron brings an editorial, bookish hand, with curves that lighten mildly toward their ends. Kameron's classic serif shapes do the careful reading work, while Happy Monkey skims along at constant stroke weight and handles the bold, distinctive display.
